symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot ping PC2, also in VLAN 10, on the same switch.
topology_note: SW1 access ports Fa0/1 (PC1) and Fa0/2 (PC2), both intended for VLAN 10.
show_output:
show vlan brief (SW1):
VLAN10  Sales   active  Fa0/1
(Fa0/2 not listed under VLAN10, appears under VLAN1)
show running-config interface fa0/2:
switchport access vlan 1
expected_fault: Fa0/2 was left in default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10 (VLAN mismatch on access port).
fix_steps: On SW1: interface fa0/2; switchport access vlan 10

symptom: Trunk between SW1 and SW2 is up but VLAN 20 hosts on SW2 cannot reach VLAN 20 hosts on SW1.
topology_note: Gi0/1 on both switches configured as trunk carrying VLANs 10,20,30.
show_output:
show interfaces trunk (SW1):
Gi0/1  allowed vlans: 10,30
show interfaces trunk (SW2):
Gi0/1  allowed vlans: 10,20,30
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is not in the allowed list on SW1's trunk (switchport trunk allowed vlan misconfigured).
fix_steps: On SW1: interface gi0/1; switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20

symptom: New PC plugged into Fa0/5 gets no link light response from expected VLAN; it lands in VLAN 1 traffic.
topology_note: Fa0/5 was supposed to be pre-configured for VLAN 30 (Engineering).
show_output:
show interfaces fa0/5 switchport:
Administrative Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)
expected_fault: Port never had switchport access vlan 30 applied; still default VLAN 1.
fix_steps: interface fa0/5; switchport access vlan 30; switchport mode access

symptom: Inter-VLAN routing works for VLAN 10 and 20 but VLAN 30 devices have no connectivity to anything, even the gateway.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick with sub-interfaces Gi0/0.10, Gi0/0.20, Gi0/0.30 on R1.
show_output:
show vlan brief:
VLAN30 present, Fa0/8 assigned
show ip interface brief (R1):
GigabitEthernet0/0.30 unassigned  administratively down
expected_fault: Sub-interface for VLAN 30 exists but is administratively down (no 'no shutdown' applied, or missing encapsulation).
fix_steps: interface gi0/0.30; encapsulation dot1Q 30; ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0; no shutdown

symptom: Voice VLAN phone registers but attached PC behind the phone has no network access.
topology_note: Fa0/3 configured with data VLAN 10 and voice VLAN 110 for an IP phone + PC pass-through.
show_output:
show interfaces fa0/3 switchport:
Access Mode VLAN: 10 (Sales)
Voice VLAN: none
expected_fault: Voice VLAN was never configured on the port, so the phone pulled default settings and shares the data VLAN oddly, breaking the PC's trunked path.
fix_steps: interface fa0/3; switchport voice vlan 110

symptom: Two switches show VLAN databases out of sync after a new VLAN was added on only one of them.
topology_note: SW1 and SW2 are both VTP clients/servers in domain CORP.
show_output:
show vtp status (SW1): VTP Operating Mode: Server, Configuration Revision: 5
show vtp status (SW2): VTP Operating Mode: Client, Configuration Revision: 5
expected_fault: SW2 never received the VTP update (revision numbers match but VLAN 40 is missing on SW2, indicating the trunk carrying VTP advertisements was down when the change was made).
fix_steps: Verify trunk state between SW1/SW2, then re-issue the VLAN add on the VTP server or manually add VLAN 40 on SW2 if in transparent mode

symptom: PC1 has a valid IP but cannot ping anything outside its own subnet, including the default gateway.
topology_note: PC1 192.168.1.10/24, gateway should be 192.168.1.1 on R1 Gi0/0.
show_output:
ipconfig (PC1): Default Gateway: 192.168.1.100
show ip interface brief (R1): GigabitEthernet0/0  192.168.1.1  up/up
expected_fault: PC1's configured default gateway (192.168.1.100) does not match the router's actual interface IP (192.168.1.1) - gateway mismatch.
fix_steps: Correct PC1's gateway to 192.168.1.1 (static) or fix DHCP pool's default-router entry

symptom: All PCs in VLAN 10 can ping each other but none can reach the internet or other VLANs.
topology_note: SVI for VLAN 10 configured on multilayer switch SW1.
show_output: show ip interface brief (SW1): Vlan10  192.168.10.1  administratively down  down
expected_fault: SVI (VLAN 10 interface) is administratively shut down, so it cannot act as gateway.
fix_steps: interface vlan10; no shutdown

symptom: PC in VLAN 20 can ping its own gateway but not devices in VLAN 10.
topology_note: SW1 is Layer 3 switch with SVIs for VLAN 10 and 20; ip routing should be enabled.
show_output:
show ip route (SW1): (no entries for connected VLAN 10/20, only C 0.0.0.0/0)
show running-config | include ip routing: (no output)
expected_fault: 'ip routing' is not enabled globally on the multilayer switch, so it behaves as a pure Layer 2 device and never routes between SVIs.
fix_steps: Global config: ip routing

symptom: DHCP client on VLAN 30 obtains an IP but the gateway field is blank, causing all off-subnet traffic to fail.
topology_note: DHCP pool VLAN30POOL configured on router R1.
show_output:
show running-config | section dhcp pool VLAN30POOL:
network 192.168.30.0 255.255.255.0
dns-server 192.168.30.1
(no default-router line)
expected_fault: DHCP pool is missing the 'default-router' statement, so clients never learn a gateway.
fix_steps: ip dhcp pool VLAN30POOL; default-router 192.168.30.1

symptom: Static-IP server can reach local subnet but times out reaching anything routed, despite gateway being pingable.
topology_note: Server has static IP 10.10.10.50/25 but the subnet is actually /24.
show_output:
ipconfig: IPv4 Address 10.10.10.50, Subnet Mask 255.255.255.128
Router interface: 10.10.10.1/24
expected_fault: Subnet mask mismatch (/25 on host vs /24 on router) causes the host to miscalculate which addresses are local, breaking off-subnet routing decisions.
fix_steps: Correct server subnet mask to 255.255.255.0 to match the router interface

symptom: PCs in a remote VLAN never receive a DHCP-assigned IP address; they fall back to APIPA (169.254.x.x).
topology_note: DHCP server is centralized on R1; remote VLAN 40 is one hop away through SW2.
show_output:
show ip dhcp binding: (no VLAN40 entries)
show running-config interface vlan40: (no ip helper-address line)
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address' on the VLAN 40 SVI, so DHCP broadcasts never reach the centralized DHCP server.
fix_steps: interface vlan40; ip helper-address 10.0.0.1 (DHCP server address)

symptom: Half the PCs in VLAN 10 get IP addresses, the other half get 'DHCP request timed out'.
topology_note: DHCP pool VLAN10POOL is sized 192.168.10.0/28 (only 14 usable hosts) but 25 devices are online.
show_output:
show ip dhcp pool VLAN10POOL:
network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.240
Total addresses: 14  Leased: 14  Available: 0
expected_fault: DHCP pool address space is exhausted (too small a subnet mask for the number of hosts).
fix_steps: Re-size the pool: network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 (or reduce lease scope/excluded addresses)

symptom: PCs in VLAN 20 receive addresses from the wrong subnet (192.168.99.x) instead of 192.168.20.x.
topology_note: Two DHCP pools exist: VLAN20POOL and a leftover TESTPOOL both matching overlapping ranges.
show_output:
show ip dhcp pool:
Pool TESTPOOL  network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0 (duplicate, wrong gateway 192.168.99.1)
Pool VLAN20POOL network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: A stale duplicate DHCP pool (TESTPOOL) overlaps the real VLAN20POOL and is being served instead, handing out the wrong gateway.
fix_steps: no ip dhcp pool TESTPOOL (remove the duplicate/legacy pool)

symptom: A specific PC always gets the same IP as a printer, causing intermittent connectivity for both.
topology_note: Printer has a static IP 192.168.10.50 inside the DHCP pool's active range.
show_output: show ip dhcp conflict: 192.168.10.50  Ping conflict
expected_fault: Static IP for the printer (192.168.10.50) was never excluded from the DHCP pool, so the DHCP server also leases it out (duplicate IP).
fix_steps: ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.50 192.168.10.50

symptom: No PC in VLAN 50 receives an IP at all, and there is no DHCP conflict or binding logged.
topology_note: VLAN 50 is a newly added branch VLAN; router should be running the DHCP service.
show_output: show running-config | section dhcp: (service dhcp is missing / 'no service dhcp' present)
expected_fault: DHCP service is globally disabled on the router ('no service dhcp'), so no pool responds anywhere, not just VLAN 50.
fix_steps: Global config: service dhcp

symptom: PCs can ping the file server by IP address but 'ping fileserver.corp.local' fails to resolve.
topology_note: DNS server address is set via DHCP option; internal DNS record should exist for fileserver.corp.local.
show_output:
ipconfig /all: DNS Servers: 192.168.1.53
nslookup fileserver.corp.local: server can't find fileserver.corp.local: NXDOMAIN
expected_fault: The A record for fileserver.corp.local does not exist on the DNS server (missing/incorrect DNS zone record), not a connectivity problem.
fix_steps: Add/correct the A record for fileserver.corp.local on the DNS server

symptom: Web browsing to external sites fails by name, but pinging 8.8.8.8 works fine.
topology_note: DHCP pool for VLAN 10 issues addressing to client PCs.
show_output:
show ip dhcp pool VLAN10POOL:
network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0
default-router 192.168.10.1
(no dns-server line)
expected_fault: DHCP pool never specifies a dns-server, so clients have no DNS resolver configured, even though IP connectivity is fine (classic Layer 3 works / Layer 7 fails split).
fix_steps: ip dhcp pool VLAN10POOL; dns-server 8.8.8.8 192.168.10.1

symptom: One specific PC cannot resolve any names while every other PC on the same VLAN works fine.
topology_note: PC uses a static IP configuration rather than DHCP.
show_output:
ipconfig /all (affected PC): DNS Servers: 127.0.0.1
Other PCs: DNS Servers: 192.168.1.53
expected_fault: This PC was statically configured to use itself (127.0.0.1) as its DNS server instead of the real DNS server.
fix_steps: Set the PC's DNS server to 192.168.1.53 (or enable DHCP)

symptom: Internal name resolution works but external domains ('www.example.com') never resolve.
topology_note: Internal DNS server 192.168.1.53 is authoritative for corp.local only and should forward externally.
show_output: show running-config on DNS router: ip name-server 192.168.1.53 (no forwarder/root hints configured on 192.168.1.53)
expected_fault: Internal DNS server has no forwarder configured for external queries, so it can answer only internal corp.local records.
fix_steps: Configure a forwarder (e.g., 8.8.8.8) on the internal DNS server for non-authoritative domains

symptom: Branch router R2's LAN (192.168.2.0/24) cannot reach HQ router R1's LAN (192.168.1.0/24) over the WAN link.
topology_note: R1 and R2 connected via serial link 10.0.0.0/30, running static routes.
show_output:
show ip route (R1): (no route to 192.168.2.0/24)
show running-config | include ip route: ip route 192.168.3.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2
expected_fault: Static route on R1 points to the wrong destination network (192.168.3.0 instead of 192.168.2.0) - typo in the route statement.

symptom: OSPF neighbors between R1 and R2 never reach FULL state; routes are missing.
topology_note: R1 area 0 process 1, R2 area 0 process 1, connected via Gi0/0.
show_output:
show ip ospf neighbor: (empty)
show running-config (R1): router ospf 1; network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 0
show running-config (R2): router ospf 1; network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 1
expected_fault: Area mismatch: R1 advertises the link in area 0 while R2 advertises it in area 1, so OSPF adjacency never forms.
fix_steps: On R2: correct the network statement's area to area 0 to match R1

symptom: Traffic from VLAN 10 to the internet works, but return traffic for a specific subnet (192.168.99.0/24) never arrives.
topology_note: R1 is the edge router with a default route to the ISP and internal static routes.
show_output: show ip route: S 192.168.99.0/24 [1/0] via 192.168.1.254 (192.168.1.254 does not exist on this network)
expected_fault: Static route for 192.168.99.0/24 points to a next-hop IP (192.168.1.254) that is not a real, reachable device on that subnet.
fix_steps: Correct the static route's next-hop to the actual next-hop router interface IP

symptom: After adding a new router R3 to the topology, R1 can no longer reach R2's LAN at all (previously worked).
topology_note: R1 - R3 - R2 chain; R1 has a static default route to R3.
show_output: show ip route (R3): (missing route toward R2's LAN, R3 only has connected routes, no routing protocol or static route configured)
expected_fault: R3, the new transit router, has no routing protocol or static routes configured, so it silently drops traffic destined beyond its directly connected interfaces.
fix_steps: Configure OSPF (or static routes) on R3 to advertise/route toward R2's LAN and the R1 side

symptom: Ping from R1 to R2's loopback succeeds, but traceroute shows the path flapping between two paths and occasional timeouts.
topology_note: R1 and R2 have two equal-cost OSPF paths via two links, one of which has a duplex mismatch.
show_output:
show interfaces gi0/1 (R1): half-duplex, 100Mb/s
show interfaces gi0/1 (R2, other end): full-duplex, 100Mb/s
input errors: 1345, CRC: 998
expected_fault: Duplex mismatch on one of the two equal-cost links causes high CRC/input errors, leading to intermittent packet loss on that path.
fix_steps: Set both ends of the link to the same duplex/speed (preferably auto/auto or full/full matching)

symptom: A newly added summarized route to Area 2 is not appearing in R1's routing table even though OSPF neighbors show FULL.
topology_note: R2 is an ABR summarizing 192.168.40.0/22 into area 0 toward R1.
show_output: show running-config (R2): area 2 range 192.168.40.0 255.255.255.0 (mask too specific for the intended /22 summary)
expected_fault: The OSPF area range mask is wrong (/24 instead of the intended /22), so the summary does not cover all the subordinate subnets, and some routes are missing.
fix_steps: Correct the area range: area 2 range 192.168.40.0 255.255.252.0

symptom: PC in VLAN 10 can ping the file server (192.168.30.10) but cannot open any file shares or web pages hosted there.
topology_note: ACL 101 applied inbound on R1's VLAN 30 interface to restrict access to the server subnet.
show_output:
show access-lists 101:
10 permit icmp any host 192.168.30.10
20 deny ip any any (implicit style, blocks TCP)
expected_fault: ACL 101 only permits ICMP to the server and denies everything else, including the TCP ports needed for file sharing/HTTP (Layer 3/4 filtering issue).
fix_steps: Add explicit permit lines for the needed TCP ports (e.g., permit tcp any host 192.168.30.10 eq 445, eq 80) before the deny

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi users can reach the internal file server, violating the intended guest-isolation policy.
topology_note: ACL GUEST-ACL should be applied to the guest VLAN 60 interface to block RFC1918 destinations.
show_output:
show running-config interface vlan60: (no ip access-group applied)
show access-lists GUEST-ACL: (ACL exists with correct deny statements)
expected_fault: The GUEST-ACL access list is correctly written but was never applied to the VLAN 60 interface (ip access-group missing).
fix_steps: interface vlan60; ip access-group GUEST-ACL in

symptom: Remote admin cannot SSH into R1 from the management VLAN even though credentials are correct and R1 is reachable via ping.
topology_note: VTY lines protected by access-class ADMIN-ACL.
show_output:
show access-lists ADMIN-ACL:
10 permit tcp host 192.168.5.20 any eq 22 (source/destination reversed)
show running-config | section line vty: access-class ADMIN-ACL in
expected_fault: The ACL entry has source and destination reversed - it should permit traffic FROM the admin host TO the router, but as written it only matches traffic sourced from port 22, not destined to it.
fix_steps: Rewrite: permit tcp host 192.168.5.20 host <R1-mgmt-ip> eq 22

symptom: After applying a new ACL to block a malicious subnet, ALL traffic through R1 stopped, including legitimate internal traffic.
topology_note: ACL 110 applied outbound on Gi0/0 (main uplink).
show_output:
show access-lists 110:
10 deny ip 203.0.113.0 0.0.0.255 any
(no permit statements follow)
expected_fault: ACL 110 has only a deny statement and relies on the implicit 'deny any any' at the end, so it blocks everything instead of just the intended subnet.
fix_steps: Add 'permit ip any any' as the final line after the specific deny statement

symptom: Internal PCs can ping internal servers but cannot reach any internet address; ISP link itself pings fine from the router.
topology_note: R1 configured for PAT (NAT overload) toward the ISP interface.
show_output:
show ip nat translations: (empty)
show running-config | include ip nat: ip nat inside source list 1 interface gi0/1 overload
show running-config interface gi0/0: (missing 'ip nat inside')
expected_fault: The inside LAN interface (Gi0/0) is missing the 'ip nat inside' command, so NAT never triggers for internal traffic even though the overload statement exists.
fix_steps: interface gi0/0; ip nat inside

symptom: Internal web server with a static NAT mapping is unreachable from outside, though it works fine internally.
topology_note: Static NAT should map public 203.0.113.10 to internal 192.168.1.100:80.
show_output:
show running-config | include ip nat inside source static: ip nat inside source static tcp 192.168.1.100 8080 203.0.113.10 80
(internal server actually listens on port 80, not 8080)
expected_fault: Static NAT rule maps the wrong internal port (8080) while the server listens on 80, so translated connections reach the host on the wrong port and are refused.
fix_steps: Correct the static NAT: ip nat inside source static tcp 192.168.1.100 80 203.0.113.10 80

symptom: NAT overload works for most internal hosts, but one subnet (192.168.50.0/24) never gets translated and can't reach the internet.
topology_note: NAT ACL 1 defines which internal networks are eligible for the overload pool.
expected_fault: The NAT source ACL (ACL 1) never includes the 192.168.50.0/24 network, so PAT never matches and translates traffic from that subnet.
fix_steps: access-list 1 permit 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255

symptom: Laptops can see the corporate SSID and associate, but never get past 'obtaining IP address'.
topology_note: WLAN mapped to VLAN 15 on the WLC/AP; DHCP relay expected on VLAN 15 SVI.
show_output:
show running-config interface vlan15: (no ip helper-address configured)
WLAN summary: SSID CORP-WIFI, interface vlan15, status enabled
expected_fault: Same root cause pattern as wired DHCP relay issues: VLAN 15's SVI is missing 'ip helper-address', so wireless DHCP requests never reach the DHCP server.
fix_steps: interface vlan15; ip helper-address 10.0.0.1

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi devices connect but roam between two APs and repeatedly drop connectivity for a few seconds.
topology_note: AP1 and AP2 cover overlapping areas on the same SSID but different channels.
show_output:
AP1: channel 6, power level 5 (max)
AP2: channel 6, power level 5 (max)
(co-channel interference between overlapping APs)
expected_fault: Both APs are set to the same channel (6) with overlapping coverage, causing co-channel interference and roaming drops.
fix_steps: Set AP2 to a non-overlapping channel (e.g., 1 or 11) and consider reducing power to limit overlap

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi users can reach the internal file server directly by IP, bypassing the intended guest isolation.
topology_note: Same as C028 but from the wireless side - guest SSID mapped to VLAN 60.
show_output:
WLAN summary: SSID GUEST-WIFI, interface vlan60
show running-config interface vlan60: ip access-group GUEST-ACL in (ACL present but GUEST-ACL itself only lists 'permit ip any any')
expected_fault: The GUEST-ACL is applied correctly to VLAN 60 but its rules were edited to a blanket permit, so it no longer actually restricts guest traffic (security/isolation issue).
fix_steps: Rewrite GUEST-ACL to deny RFC1918 destination ranges and permit only internet-bound traffic
